signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry vs Geopolitical Tension
signals.text: Iranian state media reports an oil tanker caught fire east of the Strait of Hormuz, injecting geopolitical supply risks alongside WTI trading at $93.8/bbl. USD/JPY trades at 158.42, holding above its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 157.49/157.69/158.48. In the options space, 25d risk reversals sit at an extreme -1.80 put skew, reflecting active hedging against downside despite JPY leveraged funds net short -30,379 (90th percentile, WoW -13,570). Fed SOFR 3.87% vs BoJ TONA 1.23% maintains a +264bp carry advantage favoring USD, keeping the underlying trend supported while VIX at 15.2 (17th percentile) remains well below the panic threshold required to trigger broad safe-haven flows. 160.00 remains the key level that has previously triggered BoJ verbal warnings, with official intervention risk escalating on any sustained break above that barrier. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY; carry advantage dominates while equity volatility stays contained. Catalyst: BoJ interest rate decision on 30 Oct. Risk: VIX surges above 25 or coordinated FX intervention forces a rapid unwind of spec shorts toward the 157.49 moving-average support.

signals.title: EUR/USD — Positioning Exhaustion + Vol Skew
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1197, positioned below its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.1344/1.1499/1.1600. CFTC positioning shows leveraged funds net short -84,775 contracts (week ending Oct 6) at the 4th percentile of its 52-week range (z -1.64), marking an extended institutional short. Options markets reflect heavy protection demand, with 1M ATM implied volatility at 6.5% vs 30-day realized volatility of 4.0%, generating an elevated +2.5% vol risk premium. Meanwhile, retail sentiment is 85% long, directly diverging from institutional positioning and warning of capitulation risk. Fed SOFR 3.87% vs ECB €STR 2.44% provides a +143bp carry advantage favoring USD, structurally capping upside rallies. Trade bias: Bearish EUR/USD; persistent policy divergence and negative technical momentum limit corrective rebounds. Catalyst: next ECB meeting (mkt: 88.0% hold priced) on 29 Oct. Risk: Leveraged funds trigger a short squeeze above the 20-day SMA at 1.1344.

signals.title: AUD/USD — RBA Hawkish Divergence vs Yield Drag
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6985, remaining below its daily SMA20/50/200 cluster at 0.7024/0.7091/0.7039. The RBA minutes delivered a distinctly hawkish tone, reinforcing RBA AONIA 4.60% vs Fed SOFR 3.87% to maintain a -73bp carry premium supporting the Aussie. However, Leveraged Funds net long exposure sits at +48,911 contracts (70.3% long) after paring -6,203 contracts WoW, pointing to institutional momentum deceleration. Furthermore, the US 5Y yield gained +24bp over 20D (FRED, as of Oct 8), driven by real yields (+33bp) against breakevens (-9bp), anchoring broad dollar resilience. Options skew reflects ongoing caution with 25d risk reversals at -0.97 favoring AUD puts. Trade bias: Neutral/range AUD/USD; cash carry support is offset by technical resistance at the 0.7024/0.7039 moving-average band. Catalyst: Australia Employment Change on 14 Oct. Risk: A downside surprise in Australian employment pushes spot below the 0.6900 figure.
evidence: RBA AONIA 4.60% vs Fed SOFR 3.87% — 73bp AUD premium

signals.title: GBP/USD — Cross-Asset Vol Divergence + Resistance
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3249, capped beneath its SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3280/1.3435/1.3440. Fed SOFR 3.87% vs BoE SONIA 3.73% maintains a modest +14bp carry advantage in favor of USD. Across the broader macro complex, the MOVE index sits at the 94th percentile of its trailing year at 100.7 while equity VIX remains subdued at the 17th percentile (15.2), indicating bond markets are pricing acute rate uncertainty that equity volatility has not yet reflected. CFTC data shows speculative accounts rebuilt length by +11,440 contracts WoW to net long +6,063, though 52-week percentile remains depressed at 8 (z -1.48). Trade bias: Neutral/bearish GBP/USD; heavy technical overhead at 1.3280 restrains recovery attempts. Catalyst: UK GDP release on 14 Oct. Risk: A daily close above the 20-day SMA at 1.3280 opens a path toward 1.3435.
